summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö from circa 1940 to 1959, and taught students including Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Tulku Hungkar Dorje.

Domenico Pezzi was an Italian linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia (c. 1861–1865), later holding several posts there, including professor of comparative classical and Romance linguistics from 1891.

Dominic Goodall works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 1995. His posts include Junior Research Fellow at Wolfson College, Oxford, and Professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 2000.

Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano, and held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Marion Rastelli in 2022, lecturing there in 2023, and became a postdoctoral researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2024.

Dominik Schröder worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt, taught at the Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule SVD St. Augustin (1952–1974), and was Professor of Ethnology at Nanzan University (1960–1969).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist who earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford in 1982. He held long-term posts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (circa 1984–2011) and University College London (2002–2009).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from circa 1979 to 1984. He joined the faculty of the University of California, Los Angeles, circa 1986.

Dominique-Sila Khan worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Paris-Sorbonne University from circa 1985 to 1990 and served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester before becoming Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem circa 1972.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (circa 1899–1929), and held a post at the University of London (circa 1918–1936).

Donald A. Ringe specializes in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill in 1984 and joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang in 1975 and joined the faculty at the University of Massachusetts Amherst circa 1976.

Donald Eric Capps was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees at Yale and the University of Chicago. He taught at Phillips University (1976–1981) and served as Professor of Pastoral Theology at Princeton Theological Seminary from 1981 to 2009.
Donald Ferguson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at Denmark Hill Grammar School, Regent's Park College, and University College London.
Donald Harper is a scholar of sinology. He held a post at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai, he held long-term posts at Swarthmore College (circa 1970–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University from 1955.
Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who completed his doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis in 1964. He served as department chair at Emory University from 1982 to 1988.
